STEP 2 - Vessel: White paper-style plate/bowl, roughly 20 cm diameter (side plate). Area = 3.14 x (10)^2 ≈ 314 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: One whole apple (red skin with green patch at the stem end).

STEP 4 - Area: The apple covers roughly 25% of the vessel area (about 80 cm^2 seen from above).

STEP 5 - Volume: An apple is roughly a sphere/ellipsoid about 7-8 cm across. Treat the top-down footprint as ~80 cm^2 with height ~7 cm, giving a gross envelope of about 80 x 7 ≈ 560 ml. For a whole fruit, the bulk-density approach overstates; a whole apple of this size is about 180 g, so I use that directly as the best estimate.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole apple ≈ 180 g (fruit, whole fresh, consistent with a medium-large apple).

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw apple ≈ 52 kcal per 100 g. 180 g x 52/100 = 94 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium apple at ~180 g and ~95 kcal is plausible for a single apple on a side plate. No other food is on this plate.
